court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent were in a marriage that was allegedly forced by the respondent. The petitioner left the respondent in September 2021 and started avoiding her. The respondent filed a maintenance petition, which was allowed by the trial court with an order to pay Rs.25,000/- per month.

legal_principles.principle: A certificate issued in regard to a marriage by any entity is of no legal consequence if there is no consummation of the marriage.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that, in the absence of any marriage in accordance with Section 7 of the Hindu Marriage Act, a certificate issued in that regard by any entity is of no legal consequence.
cited_cases: Dolly Rani Vs. Manish Kumar Chanchal, (2024) SCC OnLineSC 754

legal_principles.principle: A marriage is void if there is no consummation of the marriage.
legal_principles.held: Since there is no consummation of marriage between them, it is a void marriage and the petitioner is not liable to pay any maintenance to the respondent.

outcome.final_order: The final court order affirmed the decision of the trial court and rejected the petitioner's appeal.

use_for_drafting: assisting in a family court case
